title: Repeated Game Strategy
body_html:
Repeated Game Strategy

In a standard repeated game, a strategy of player $i$ is a map $$ \sigma_i:H\to\Delta(A_i), $$ where $H=\bigcup_{t\ge 0}H_t$ is the set of finite public histories.

After history $h\in H_t$, the mixed action $\sigma_i(h)$ is used at stage $t+1$. A strategy profile induces a probability distribution on finite histories and, by extension, on infinite plays.

References

  • [MFoGT, Chapter 8, Definition 8.3.1] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MechDesign.pdf. Behavior strategies in standard repeated games.
